# OBS012 `shared-do-termination`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

Several `do` loops end on the same labelled statement.

## Why

Nested loops sharing one terminal statement (deleted in Fortran 2018) make jumps to the label
ambiguous and hide the nesting structure. Give each loop its own `end do`.

## Reported

```fortran
do 10 i = 1, n
do 10 j = 1, m
10 a(i, j) = 0.0
```

## Preferred

```fortran
do i = 1, n
  do j = 1, m
    a(i, j) = 0.0
  end do
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS012] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS012` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB092` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
